name: Diphenhydramine
toxicities: fatal at amounts close to or exceeding 2 grams
summary: An antihistamine which, when taken in smaller doses relieves allergies and insomnia. In larger doses works as a deliriant and can actually keep the user awake. Generally the 'high' of this drug is reported as dysphoric, potentially causing hallucinations indistinguishable from reality.
generalRisks: The DailyMed OTC oral sleep-aid label warns that diphenhydramine causes drowsiness, should not be used with alcohol, and can impair driving and machinery operation. It advises against use in children under 12 or with any other diphenhydramine-containing product, including topical products, and recommends asking a clinician before use with breathing problems, glaucoma, urinary difficulty, sedatives, or tranquilizers. Overdose requires immediate medical help.
saferUse: Avoid alcohol and do not drive or operate machinery after use.
Do not combine with other diphenhydramine-containing products, including topical products; ask a clinician before combining with sedatives or tranquilizers.
The cited OTC label says not to use under age 12 and to seek medical advice if sleeplessness lasts more than two weeks. In overdose, contact emergency medical help or Poison Control immediately.
metabolism: Evidence is from Benylin Chesty Coughs (Original), which contains diphenhydramine with menthol. Diphenhydramine and menthol are well absorbed from the gut after oral administration, with peak serum levels of diphenhydramine reached between 2 and 2.5 hours after a 50 mg oral dose. It is widely distributed throughout the body, including the CNS; the volume of distribution after 50 mg orally is 3.3-6.8 l/kg and it is some 78% bound to plasma proteins. Diphenhydramine undergoes extensive first-pass metabolism: two successive N-demethylations occur, with the resultant amine then oxidised to a carboxylic acid. Plasma clearance of a 50 mg oral dose lies in the range 600-1300 ml/min and the terminal elimination half-life in the range 3.4-9.3 hours. Little unchanged drug is excreted in the urine.
